subject.title: fix(agents): memoize exec auto-reviewer verdicts for identical requests (#102249)

question: May a completed low-risk model exec-review verdict be reused within one reviewer lifetime when—and only when—the full canonical execution identity, including the resolved executable, is unchanged?
rationale: Reusing an authorization-adjacent model verdict trades provider cost for less frequent security review, so the permanent cache identity and reuse contract require explicit owner acceptance.

options.title: Cache canonical execution identity
options.body: Allow bounded per-reviewer reuse only after the key includes the resolved executable and every prompt and execution-binding security fact.

options.title: Keep per-exec model review
options.body: Reject verdict memoization and preserve a fresh model review for every approval-requiring execution despite the additional provider cost.

options.title: Optimize outside authorization
options.body: Avoid verdict reuse and pursue provider prompt caching or another billing optimization that does not cache an authorization-adjacent decision.

recommendation.title: Cache canonical execution identity
recommendation.body: Allow bounded per-reviewer reuse only after the key includes the resolved executable and every prompt and execution-binding security fact.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository ownership guidance assigns the agents and subagents surface to Tyler, and this choice directly affects the shared agent exec-review boundary.
